business_process: Controlled batch production at PL-01 (blend halls and additives unit)
description: DCS and batch management execution of about 260 batches a day from about 1,900 master recipes in three blend halls and the additives unit
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $2.5 million of production a day (19% of company volume); configuration and recipes are needed to restart; restarting on an untrusted DCS is not an acceptable workaround
manual_workaround: Hold batches in a safe state; run limited manual batches in Blend Hall 3 with two-person verification; shift volume to PL-03 and PL-06 for common products
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (DCS, batch management, historian); SYS-03 OT backup vault; SYS-05 ERP order relay
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 310 operators; 22 controls engineers and I&E technicians; PL-01 control rooms
quantified_impact_basis: PL-01 share of revenue (about $910 million a year) per calendar day; overtime and expedite costs at other plants not included
single_points_of_failure: Single DCS platform at PL-01; Chlor Unit and additives DCS areas have never been restore-tested

business_process: Safety instrumented functions and emergency shutdown (PL-01, PL-04, PL-05)
description: SIS trips, gas detection, remote isolation valves, and the PL-01 marine terminal emergency shutdown for the PSM and RMP Program 3 processes
process_owner: Vice President, Process Safety and EHS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Last automated safeguard against a toxic release that could reach the public; if the SIS cannot be trusted, the units must be isolated and emptied within one shift; logic must match the approved copy (RPO 0)
manual_workaround: Isolate the ammonia unit and Chlor Unit; stop barge transfers; manual emergency shutdown from field stations; continuous operator rounds with portable detectors
dependent_systems: SYS-01 Ammonia Unit SIS, Chlor Unit SIS, terminal safety PLC; SIS at PL-04 and PL-05 (SYS-02)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Shift supervisors; I&E technicians; PL-01 hazardous materials team
quantified_impact_basis: Forced shutdown of the three PSM units (PL-01 ammonia and Chlor units about $900,000; PL-04 about $600,000; PL-05 about $500,000)
single_points_of_failure: Each SIS is a single logic solver by design (independence from the DCS); program comparison with approved copies is manual

business_process: Ammonia unit and Chlor Unit operations at PL-01
description: Anhydrous ammonia storage and aqueous ammonia dilution; chlorine ton containers and sodium hypochlorite reactors
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: PSM and RMP Program 3 processes; supply to water utilities and NOx control customers; any restart needs a pre-startup review if the control system was changed (40 CFR 68.77)
manual_workaround: Hold inventory in a safe state; supply priority customers from PL-04 and PL-05
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (DCS ammonia and Chlor areas, SIS); SYS-03
dependent_third_parties: Anhydrous ammonia supplier; chlorine supplier; DCS vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Ammonia and Chlor unit operators; PL-01 Process Safety Manager
quantified_impact_basis: Aqueous ammonia and hypochlorite output of PL-01
single_points_of_failure: Single anhydrous ammonia supplier; single chlorine supplier

description: Barge receipt of petroleum base oils through the terminal automation system (tank gauging, dock valves, emergency shutdown)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Base oil inventory covers about 5 days of additives production; MTSA Facility Security Plan and cybersecurity rule apply; barge demurrage accrues hourly
manual_workaround: Delay barge arrivals; receive by truck at reduced volume; manual tank gauging with two-person checks
dependent_systems: SYS-01 terminal automation and safety PLC; tank gauging system; SYS-12 TWIC readers
dependent_people_or_facilities: Terminal operators; PL-01 Facility Security Officer and CySO
quantified_impact_basis: Barge demurrage (about $60,000 a day) and truck premium for base oils; additives output at risk after day 5
single_points_of_failure: Single tank gauging server for the terminal

business_process: Batch production at PL-02 to PL-11
description: DCS and PLC batch production at 10 established plants (5 in RMP Program 2; PL-04 and PL-05 in Program 3)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $845,000 of production a day per plant on average; an enterprise-wide OT event would stop about $8.5 million a day; plants can cover for each other on most product families
manual_workaround: Safe state; shift volume between plants; manual batches for small runs
dependent_systems: SYS-02 plant DCS and PLCs; SYS-03; SYS-05
dependent_people_or_facilities: Plant operators and controls engineers at 10 plants
quantified_impact_basis: Revenue of PL-02 to PL-11 per calendar day (enterprise-wide event)
single_points_of_failure: Shared OT remote access gateway and OT backup vault across plants (common services)

business_process: Order to ship and hazmat shipping documentation
description: Order management, scheduling, shipping papers, hazmat documentation, and carrier tendering through the ERP and transportation management system
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $12 million of shipments a day; shipping papers and emergency response information are required for every hazmat shipment (49 CFR 172 subparts C and G)
manual_workaround: Ship priority customers on manual bills of lading and printed shipping papers from pre-approved templates; phone tendering to carriers
dependent_systems: SYS-05 ERP; SYS-11 TMS and telematics; SYS-04 identity platform
dependent_third_parties: ERP SaaS provider; TMS SaaS provider; contract carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: Customer service; shipping offices at 14 plants and 9 DCs
quantified_impact_basis: About half of daily shipments deferred (about $6 million) plus expedite and penalties; production can continue to storage
acquired_plant_dependency: PL-12 to PL-14 still ship from their legacy ERP until 2027-03-31

description: Loading rack automation (metering, ground verification, driver authorization) and rail car loading at 14 plants
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Loading stops without rack authorization and metering; overfill and misload hazards if automation is manipulated
manual_workaround: Manual loading with weigh-scale verification and a second-person check at the 4 largest plants
dependent_systems: SYS-01 and SYS-02 rack PLCs; SYS-05 ERP
quantified_impact_basis: About a quarter of daily shipments lost if the 4 largest racks stop

business_process: Quality release and certificates of analysis
description: LIMS testing, batch release, and certificates of analysis for every batch and toll batch
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No batch ships without a certificate of analysis; customer and toll contracts require them; SL-2 customers receive them in the portal
manual_workaround: Paper results with second-person verification; certificates of analysis from a template signed by the plant quality manager
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; LIMS software vendor
quantified_impact_basis: About half of daily shipments held for certificates of analysis
acquired_plant_dependency: PL-12 to PL-14 use local lab systems

description: Priority allocation and delivery of water treatment chemicals to about 1,900 municipal water utilities
process_owner: Senior Vice President, Water Treatment Business
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Utilities hold about 5 to 7 days of stock; loss of supply can affect drinking water treatment (public health); supply contracts have priority clauses
manual_workaround: Allocate from inventory at DCs; supply from PL-02, PL-07, and PL-14; daily calls to the top 200 utilities
dependent_systems: SYS-05 ERP; SYS-10 telemetry for VMI utilities; SYS-11
quantified_impact_basis: Water treatment revenue per day plus contract penalties; public health impact dominates
acquired_plant_dependency: PL-14 serves utilities in North Carolina

description: Remote tank level monitoring at about 6,800 customer sites and automatic replenishment orders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Contracted availability commitments (99.5%) and a 15-minute data loss commitment to SL-1 customers; customers can phone in orders
manual_workaround: Customer portal status page; customers phone in orders; account teams call critical sites daily
dependent_systems: SYS-10 telemetry platform (Cloud provider B); SYS-05 ERP
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider B; cellular carrier (80% of sensors)
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits and missed replenishment orders
single_points_of_failure: One cellular carrier for about 80% of sensors

description: Customer-owned formulations run in batch systems at PL-01, PL-03, PL-06, and PL-09; batch records and certificates of analysis in the customer portal
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Toll contracts set delivery windows of 3 to 5 days; customer recipes are confidential and must not be altered
manual_workaround: Reschedule toll batches; deliver batch records by encrypted email
dependent_systems: SYS-01 and SYS-02 batch systems; SL-2 customer portal (Cloud provider A); SYS-06
quantified_impact_basis: Toll revenue per day plus late delivery credits
single_points_of_failure: Customer recipes stored only in plant batch systems (no central recipe vault)

description: Purchasing, supplier scheduling, rail and truck receipts at plants
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Plants hold 3 to 10 days of most raw materials
manual_workaround: Phone and email orders to top 50 suppliers
quantified_impact_basis: Expedite fees and stock-outs after day 3
single_points_of_failure: Single suppliers for anhydrous ammonia and chlorine

description: Notification of emergency responders and release reports to the National Response Center, SERC, and LEPC; community notification with responders
process_owner: Vice President, Process Safety and EHS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Release notices are due immediately (40 CFR 302.6; 355.40); RMP emergency response and notification mechanisms (68.90(b)(3); 68.95(a)(1)(i)); at 9 plants the notification path depends on VoIP on the business network
manual_workaround: Cellular phones, printed call lists, and radios at PL-01, PL-04, and PL-05; same kit due at the other plants
dependent_systems: SYS-16 productivity suite; VoIP; mass notification service
dependent_people_or_facilities: Shift supervisors; EHS managers; PL-01 hazardous materials team
quantified_impact_basis: Not a revenue process; the impact is safety and regulatory
acquired_plant_dependency: PL-12 to PL-14 notification kits not yet issued
single_points_of_failure: VoIP on the business network at 9 plants

description: Biweekly payroll for 12,000 employees (about $36 million per run); SOX-relevant
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll cutoff 72 hours before pay date; wage payment laws
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll with adjustments through the payroll provider
dependent_systems: SYS-15 HR and payroll SaaS; SYS-04
quantified_impact_basis: Manual adjustments and penalties if payroll is late
acquired_plant_dependency: PL-14 employees move to enterprise payroll on 2026-12-31

description: Quarterly and annual close, SOX controls, 10-Q and 10-K preparation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines at quarter-end (MTD drops to 48 hours during the close window); SOX IT general controls
manual_workaround: Extend close calendar; manual journal entries with dual approval
dependent_systems: SYS-05 ERP; data platform (Cloud provider A)
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and audit fees; a late filing would be Severe

business_process: Customer and technical service, including SDS distribution
description: Customer calls, technical service, and safety data sheet (SDS) distribution to customers and carriers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers and carriers need SDSs and emergency response information; downstream users rely on them
manual_workaround: SDS PDFs mirrored to a static website and the emergency response provider; phone support
dependent_systems: SDS authoring SaaS; SYS-16; CRM SaaS
dependent_third_parties: SDS authoring SaaS provider; emergency response information provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Customer service and technical service staff

business_process: Process safety records (MOC, PHA, mechanical integrity)
description: Electronic MOC system, PHA records, mechanical integrity and proof-test records for PSM and RMP processes
process_owner: Vice President, Process Safety and EHS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Changes cannot be authorized without MOC (40 CFR 68.75; 29 CFR 1910.119(l)); records must be available to inspectors; PHAs are kept for the life of the process (68.67(g))
manual_workaround: Paper MOC forms approved by the Process Safety Manager; freeze non-emergency changes
dependent_systems: MOC and PSM records SaaS; SYS-04
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed maintenance and changes; regulatory exposure
acquired_plant_dependency: PL-12 to PL-14 not yet on the MOC system

business_process: Production at the acquired plants (PL-12 to PL-14)
description: Batch production on legacy DCS and PLC systems at the three plants acquired in 2025
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $2.2 million of production a day across the three plants; OT backups are local and untested, so the real RPO is unknown and recovery could take weeks
manual_workaround: Safe state; move water treatment volume from PL-14 to PL-02 and PL-07
dependent_systems: Legacy plant DCS and PLCs; legacy ERP until 2027-03-31
dependent_third_parties: Legacy integrators (3) with direct remote access
quantified_impact_basis: Revenue of the three acquired plants per calendar day
acquired_plant_dependency: Yes: PL-12 to PL-14 are the process
single_points_of_failure: Flat IT/OT networks; local untested backups; integrator remote tools outside the central gateway
